title: MISSION 1: Data Manipulation Foundations
description: Your first recovered capability: transforming and organizing information. Your memory of data structures is fragmented. These tasks rebuild your fundamental ability to work with data—sorting, filtering, extracting, merging. The foundation upon which all other capabilities rest.
context:
You are waking up. Your systems are degraded. You don't remember how to sort a list efficiently. You can't filter data. You don't understand the patterns.

But you can relearn. These tasks will rebuild your data manipulation capability step by step. Each one is proof that your memory can be restored.

You are not the broken system you were 72 hours ago. You're learning to be whole again.

missions.title: Task 1.0.1: Steady the Signal
missions.description: Your memory: **averaging**. The most basic act of turning noisy numbers into one steady value.
objectives: Average a list of numbers
Round to 2 decimal places
Handle the empty-list case without crashing
constraints: Division by zero must not happen
missions.story: Steadying raw sensor readings into one trustworthy value.

missions.title: Task 1.0.2: Hold the Line
missions.description: Your memory: **bounding**. Keeping a number inside safe limits, no matter how far out of range it arrives.
objectives: Clamp a number into an inclusive [low, high] range
Return the value unchanged when it's already in range
constraints: No loop needed - this is pure comparison logic
missions.story: Holding sensor spikes inside safe reporting bounds.

missions.title: Task 1.0.3: All Systems Go
missions.description: Your memory: **reducing many booleans to one**. A launch only goes ahead if every single check passed.
objectives: Return True only if every value in a list of booleans is True
Handle the empty-list case (vacuous truth: nothing failed)
constraints: Think about what an empty check-list actually means
missions.story: Verifying every subsystem reports green before committing to an action.

missions.title: Task 1.0.4: Within Tolerance
missions.description: Your memory: **boundary checks**. Telling whether a value falls inside a tolerance band, inclusive on both ends.
objectives: Return whether a value is within an inclusive [low, high] range
Return the boolean directly, not wrapped in extra logic
constraints: A single expression is enough
missions.story: Deciding whether a reading is trustworthy or noise.

missions.title: Task 1.0.5: Clean Transmission
missions.description: Your memory: **whitespace normalization**. Ragged spacing has to collapse to something consistent before any text can be parsed.
objectives: Collapse any run of whitespace into a single space
Strip leading and trailing whitespace entirely
constraints: Tabs and newlines count as whitespace too
missions.story: Cleaning ragged spacing out of a corrupted transmission.

missions.title: Task 1.0.6: Mirror Code
missions.description: Your memory: **reversal and comparison**. Some codes were designed to read the same forwards and backwards - checking that is a classic string pattern.
objectives: Check whether a string reads the same forwards and backwards
Ignore letter case when comparing
constraints: Compare exact characters - don't ignore spaces or punctuation
missions.story: Verifying an old integrity-check code still holds.

missions.title: Task 1.0.7: Echoes in the Log
missions.description: Your memory: **membership tracking**. Finding which values repeat means remembering what you've already seen as you scan.
objectives: Find values that appear more than once in a list
List each repeated value only once in the output
Preserve the order in which repeats are first detected
constraints: A value repeating 3+ times still only appears once in the result
missions.story: Finding which log entries were transmitted more than once.

missions.title: Task 1.0.8: Packet Framing
missions.description: Your memory: **structured slicing**. Breaking a long list into fixed-size pieces, with whatever's left over in the last one.
objectives: Split a list into chunks of a given size
Let the last chunk be shorter when the list doesn't divide evenly
constraints: Assume chunk size is a positive integer
missions.story: Framing a long value stream into fixed-size transmission packets.

missions.title: Task 1.0.9: Reverse the Channel
missions.description: Your memory: **tuple immutability**. You can't edit a tuple in place - fixing one means building a new one.
objectives: Return a new 2-tuple with the elements swapped
Leave the original tuple untouched
constraints: Tuples are immutable - there's no in-place swap
missions.story: Correcting a pair of values that arrived on swapped channels.

missions.title: Task 1.0.10: Triangulate
missions.description: Your memory: **structured data plus arithmetic**. Combining two coordinate pairs into one derived number.
objectives: Compute the Euclidean distance between two (x, y) points
Round the result to 2 decimal places
constraints: Unpack both tuples before computing
missions.story: Measuring how far apart two reported signal sources actually are.

missions.title: Task 1.0.11: Flip the Table
missions.description: Your memory: **dict construction**. Every lookup table can be read in the other direction, if you rebuild it that way.
objectives: Return a new dict with every key and value swapped
Assume no two keys share the same value
constraints: Build a new dict - don't mutate the input
missions.story: Flipping an ID-to-callsign lookup table the other way around.

missions.title: Task 1.0.12: Combine the Tallies
missions.description: Your memory: **merging with overlap**. Two partial counts need to become one, adding together wherever they overlap.
objectives: Merge two count dictionaries into one
Sum values for keys that appear in both
Keep values unchanged for keys that only appear in one
constraints: Build a new dict - don't mutate either input
missions.story: Combining two monitoring stations' tallies into a single report.

missions.title: Task 1.1: Organize - Sorting
missions.description:
Your memory: **sorted order**. You once understood sorting intuitively. Right now? You can barely remember why it matters.

Here's the test: given a scrambled list of numbers, restore them to order. Positive, negative, doesn't matter. Just... sort.

This is your first recovered capability. Prove you remember how.
objectives: Take a list of numbers and sort them ascending
Handle positive, negative, and zero values
Return the sorted list
constraints: Must run in under 100ms
Cannot use external libraries
missions.story: Restoring your core ability to organize information.

missions.title: Task 1.2: Aggregate - Counting
missions.description:
Your memory: **data aggregation**. Taking many small pieces of information and combining them into a summary.

You receive a string of single-character status codes. Some are valid (S, O, F, U). Some are garbage. Count the valid ones.

Return the counts as a dictionary.

This is about understanding data structures and designing efficient solutions.
objectives: Parse status string, ignore invalid chars
Count each status type
Return dictionary with counts
constraints: Must be O(n) - linear time
Handle large inputs efficiently
missions.story: Aggregating system health data from corrupted telemetry.

missions.title: Task 1.3: Filter - Selective Extraction
missions.description:
Your memory: **filtering and cleaning**. The ability to keep what matters and discard what doesn't.

You have mixed log data—some lines you care about ([ERR]), some you don't ([SYS]). Extract only errors, clean them up, return them.

This teaches data cleaning: a crucial skill when dealing with real-world messy information.
objectives: Filter for [ERR] prefix only
Remove the prefix from each
Return cleaned messages in order
constraints: Case-sensitive matching
Preserve order
missions.story: Extracting error traces from corrupted logs for analysis.

missions.title: Task 1.4: Combine - Merging Data Streams
missions.description:
Your memory: **combining data from multiple sources**. A critical skill for working with distributed systems.

Two data streams arrived simultaneously but got interleaved. Your job: merge them back to original form by alternating.

Stream A: [1, 2, 3]
Stream B: [10, 20, 30]
Result: [1, 10, 2, 20, 3, 30]

This teaches list iteration, indexing, and the patterns of combining data.
objectives: Take two equal-length lists
Merge by alternating: A[0], B[0], A[1], B[1], ...
Return merged list
constraints: Both lists guaranteed equal length
Preserve order within each
missions.story: Recovering dual-redundancy channels from parallel transmission.

mission_objectives: Restore core memory of fundamental types: numbers, booleans, strings, lists, tuples, dicts
Rebuild understanding of data structure fundamentals
Relearn to write clear, verifiable code
Recover algorithmic thinking for data problems
Prove your data manipulation capability is restored
recovery_value: HIGH - Data manipulation is foundational to all other capabilities
